questions.question: What does the repository do, and who calls or runs it?
questions.answer: ripgrep provides rg, a command-line recursive regex search tool for users and scripts. By default it respects ignore rules and skips hidden/binary inputs. Reusable searching crates are exposed through the grep library facade.

evidence.excerpt:
ripgrep (rg)
------------
ripgrep is a line-oriented search tool that recursively searches the current
directory for a regex pattern. By default, ripgrep will respect gitignore rules
and automatically skip hidden files/directories and binary files. (To disable
all automatic filtering by default, use `rg -uuu`.) ripgrep has first class
support on Windows, macOS and Linux, with binary downloads available for [every
release](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/releases). ripgrep is similar to
other popular search tools like The Silver Searcher, ack and grep.

questions.question: Name the principal components and their responsibilities.
questions.answer: crates/core coordinates CLI flags, haystacks and search workers. ignore walks files with filtering; grep is a facade over matcher/searcher/regex/printer/cli crates. SearchWorker coordinates matcher/searcher/printer, including preprocessing and decompression.

ignore walks files with filtering; grep is a facade over matcher/searcher/regex/printer/cli crates.
SearchWorker coordinates matcher/searcher/printer, including preprocessing and decompression.

evidence.excerpt:
/*!
The ignore crate provides a fast recursive directory iterator that respects
various filters such as globs, file types and `.gitignore` files. The precise
matching rules and precedence is explained in the documentation for
`WalkBuilder`.

Secondarily, this crate exposes gitignore and file type matchers for use cases
that demand more fine-grained control.

/*!
Defines a very high level "search worker" abstraction.

A search worker manages the high level interaction points between the matcher
(i.e., which regex engine is used), the searcher (i.e., how data is actually
read and matched using the regex engine) and the printer. For example, the
search worker is where things like preprocessors or decompression happens.
*/

questions.question: For rg --threads 1 PATTERN FILE with an ordinary text file and no preprocessing/indexing, give the source-supported call/dispatch path to its outcome; identify dynamic or unresolved boundaries.
questions.answer: main -> flags::parse -> run -> search; HiArgs constructs walker/haystacks and matcher/searcher/printer. SearchWorker.search -> worker search_path -> generic search_path -> Searcher.search_path with printer sink. search folds SearchResult.has_match; run maps match/error state to exit 0/1/2. Filesystem content, generic Matcher/Sink dispatch and platform I/O are runtime boundaries; this is source reachability, not an observed execution.

questions.question: Where does RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH enter and get handled or transformed?
questions.answer: flags/config.rs args reads RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH and parses the file, reporting read errors and returning no config arguments on failure. parse_reader trims lines, skips blanks/comments and converts remaining lines to OsString arguments. parse_low skips config for special modes or --no-config; otherwise config arguments precede CLI arguments in reparsing. parse converts LowArgs to HiArgs; filesystem reading is a runtime boundary.
